Can you send over Redwood's most recent penetration test report for the Hosted API surface? Our procurement team needs the executive summary and the full findings. From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Request for latest pen test + telemetry redaction options (Hosted API)

Hi Audrey — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer: yes, we can provide a redacted penetration test package and a separate telemetry export subject to agreed redaction rules and an NDA addendum for telemetry. Summary below and a proposed delivery workflow.

Scope confirmation:
- The most recent engagement (Aug 2026) covered the Hosted API front door (api.redwood.ai), authentication flows (API keys + token exchange), and the immediate ingestion/validation pipeline inside the hosted control plane. The engagement did NOT include customer-managed on-prem instances.

What we can provide:
- Executive summary PDF (redacted) + full findings PDF (sensitive sections redacted per our standard redaction policy).
- Telemetry exports limited to request metadata and aggregated timings; raw prompt text or user identifiers will be redacted or replaced with deterministic hashes per your preference.
- A remediation matrix (spreadsheet) mapping each finding to a tracked remediation and status.

Delivery methods (pick one):
1) Ephemeral S3 presigned URLs (recommended) — objects expire after N days; we can enforce server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) with a Redwood-managed KMS key or, if you prefer, a customer-provided key via an HSM workflow.
2) SFTP to a customer IP-restricted host — requires an approved IP and account setup; retention policy must be agreed.
3) Secure Share (enterprise SharePoint / Box link) with link expiration and view-only access.

Proposed redaction template for telemetry exports (options):
- Level A (minimal): remove prompt text and any 3rd-party PII; keep response latency and status codes.
- Level B (moderate): Level A + deterministic hashing of user_id and session_id; preserve request path and status codes.
- Level C (full anonymization): aggregate-only (no user/session-level records).

Planned timeline if you approve Level B + presigned S3:
- Today (10/06): confirm redaction level and delivery method.
- 10/07: internal redaction run + manager review.
- 10/08: upload to presigned S3 and send link (expires 7 days).

I've attached a redacted executive summary (redacted_pt_summary_v3.pdf) and the remediation matrix stub (remediation_matrix_Rivermark.xlsx) for context — both are placeholders until we confirm redaction level. Laura + Marissa — tagging you for compliance sign-off and any additional constraints (KMS/customer key requirement, retention window).

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redacted_pt_summary_v3.pdf (attachment stub), remediation_matrix_Rivermark.xlsx (attachment stub)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Thanks for the plan, Priyom. A few guardrails from Compliance:
- We are ok to share redacted telemetry at "Level B" only with a signed addendum that limits retention to 7 days and prohibits re-identification attempts. Please add language to the delivery email requiring confirmation that Rivermark will purge any telemetry extracts within 7 days and will not attempt to deanonymize hashes.
- Use Redwood-managed KMS key unless the customer provides a compliance-approved key and there's a PR (procurement) ticket. If they request customer-managed keys, loop in our Cloud Security team — that'll add 2–3 business days.
- All presigned objects must expire within 7 days and we should rotate presign tokens per this transfer.

Priyom — once you have the final redactions, follow the "secure-send" checklist in the internal share doc and paste the presigned URL to the recipient with the retention/addendum language.

Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference
